newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to auction five percent of LUKoil.
newsitem.headline: Russia to auction five percent of LUKoil.

text.p: Russia will hold a commercial tender for five percent of its biggest oil company OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil on June 20, the Federal Property Fund said on Monday.
The stake comprises 35.73 million shares, it said in its weekly Reforma bulletin, of which an advance copy was made available to Reuters.
Earlier this year the Russian privatisation authorities announced they would sell 15 percent of LUKoil and were considering selling an option on a further 4-5 percent.
But in late 1995 they also transferred the management of five percent of LUKoil to a consortium of LUKoil itself and Bank Imperial, under the government's shares-for-loans scheme.

It appeared that this was the stake involved. The government has recently auctioned off other stakes in oil companies originally mortgaged under the shares-for-loans programme, and the official seller of this stake is a "tender commission", as in other such sales.

At 1110 GMT LUKoil ordinaries were at $15.01, putting a value on the stake of about $535 million. LUKoil and Bank Imperial won control of the stake in late 1995 with a loan of $35.001 million. Oil company stakes mortgaged under the shares-for-loans programme which have been auctioned recently have been sold for prices barely above the original loan. --Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
